To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the eigenvector approach can be used to remove symmetries from the data even in the presence of significant noise; and (b) the eigenvectors can be used to construct a low-dimensional parametrized manifold on which the original dynamics is accurately approximated.

(1) we can successfully quotient out the symmetry degrees of freedom in the presence of noisy data (2) this can be used to effectively reduce the dimension of the dynamical system (3) this can be combined into a single step with a standard nonlinear dimensionality reduction technique.

(i) the eigenvectors of a matrix that encodes the symmetries of the dynamical system under consideration are useful for quotienting out the symmetries, even in the presence of significant noise, (ii) the eigenvector-based technique is a first step in the direction of data mining the "noise-adjusted" ensemble, and (iii) a single eigenvector-based algorithm (vector diffusion maps) combines the symmetry-removal and dimensionality reduction steps.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a systematic framework for the analysis of large noisy data sets arising from noisy dynamical systems with symmetries, with the ultimate goal of extracting a low-dimensional representation of the system's dynamics.
the development of new mathematical tools that will enable the extraction of the "essential" degrees of freedom of a dynamical system from a large ensemble of noisy snapshots of its trajectory.
the development of techniques that allow the processing of noisy data generated from high-dimensional, nonlinear dynamical systems, in the presence of symmetries.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a new technique for processing noisy data from noisy simulations, and that we have applied it to two important problems in applied mathematics and computational physics.

we demonstrate that the combination of eigenvector-based methods and diffusion maps can be used in a very general setting to extract the essential dynamics of noisy data sets, even in the presence of intrinsic symmetries.
, in the presence of symmetries, one can effectively reduce the dimension of the system, while preserving the dynamics, and that one can do this without having to know the symmetries beforehand.
The main takeaway from our work is that
symmetry reduction of noisy dynamics, which is of great practical importance, is feasible and can be performed effectively.
the eigenvector-based approach can be successfully applied even in the presence of substantial noise.
